elements.char: MR imaging is an indirect process, whereby cross-sectional images of the subject’s anatomy are
elements.label: text

elements.char: produced from frequency and phase measurements instead of direct, spatially-resolved measure-
elements.label: text

elements.char: ments.
elements.label: text

elements.char: A measuring instrument, known as a
elements.label: text

elements.char: receiver coil
elements.label: text

elements.char: , is placed in proximity to the area to
elements.label: text

elements.char: be imaged (Figure 1). During imaging, a sequence of spatially- and temporally-varying magnetic
elements.label: text

elements.char: fields, called a “pulse sequence,” is applied by the MRI machine. This induces the body to emit res-
elements.label: text

elements.char: onant electromagnetic response fields which are measured by the receiver coil. The measurements
elements.label: text

elements.char: typically correspond to points along a prescribed path through the multidimensional Fourier-space
elements.label: text

elements.char: representation of an imaged body. This Fourier space is known as
elements.label: text

elements.char: k-space
elements.label: text

elements.char: in the medical imaging
elements.label: text

elements.char: community. In the most basic usage of MR imaging, the full Fourier-space representation of a region
elements.label: text

elements.char: is captured by a sequence of samples that tile the space up to a specified maximum frequency.
elements.label: text

elements.char: A slice corresponds to one image.
